content:
Facts: Plaintiff challenged authenticity of uncle's 1996 holographic will published 2017; claimed will apocryphal based on private handwriting analysis; defendant contested claiming expert examined only signature not entire document, used limited comparison documents, failed examining both will-signatures; court-appointed expert confirmed non-authenticity through comprehensive analysis of signatures, text, comparison with contemporary and non-contemporary documents using methodologically-approved investigation.
Legal Framework: Articles 602, 606 Italian Civil Code (holographic will validity requirements; nullity); Art. 115 CPC (non-contestation principle); Art. 217(2) CPC (comparison document admissibility); case law on signature/handwriting separation (Turin 3385/2019, Cass. 20703/2013).
Interpretive Issues: Whether handwriting-body and signature constitute severable will-components for authenticity assessment; admissibility of challenging only signature authenticity while acknowledging text-handwriting; methodological requirements for graphological expert analysis selecting comparison documents; probative weight of contemporary versus temporally-distant comparison writings; whether block-letter will versus cursive comparisons prevents authenticity finding; burden allocation for apocrypha proof when defendant generically contests without analytical rebuttal.
Principles Applied: Art. 602 establishes handwriting, signature, date as essential validity requirements; presence necessary ensuring deceased-provision authenticity, complete document-authenticity assessment excluding tampering/falsification, guaranteeing statements-testator correspondence. Handwriting-signature-date constituting distinct requirements; invalidity determined by any single element absence. Will invalid upon any third-party intervention regardless of type/extent, even single-word writing during drafting. Case examined per most-liquid-reason criterion limiting verification to signature-authenticity with other issues absorbed; judgment not requiring full case-reconstruction in all legal aspects, only ascertaining conditions for requested-protection grant. Defendant's generic challenge claiming biased analysis examining only signature, not entire-document handwriting, constitutes irrelevant generic defense. Non-contestation principle application: defendant required taking clear analytical factual-position per Art. 115; counterparty limiting itself to questioning acceptance-grounds without clear specific refutation supported by appropriate Art. 2697(2) evidence renders plaintiff-alleged facts undisputed. Signatures deemed apocryphal, non-attributable to testator. Court-appointed expert constitutes perceptive technical consultation as genuine objective evidence source, not mere assessment tool. Expert viewed/analyzed/scanned original will finding intact document; comparative documents quantitatively/qualitatively exhaustive especially contemporary notarial-deed signatures. Comparison revealed structural similarities due to forger-skill but numerous significant differences concerning ductus scriptorius (general writing-style including speed, graphic stroke, letter inclination, momentum, pressure); synthetic peculiarities defining writing through movement. Forger may imitate individual-letter structure with training/predisposition but cannot imitate ductus scriptorius rhythmic-variations regarding execution-speed/fluidity specific to each writer. Will-signatures show striking differences from autographs regarding execution-speed, fluidity, momentum, writing-ingenuity, letter-inclination, graphic-continuity; written with precision/slowness not belonging to testator's personality. Expert examined both will-signatures contrary to defendant-complaint; analyzed contemporary 1996 signatures (most significant chronologically per scientific-literature) plus prior/subsequent signatures for evolution-contextualization. Block-letter/cursive difference overcome through analytical examination showing shared intrinsic handwriting-characteristics in dynamic-interaction (rhythmic-frequency repetition, systematic connotation/marking combination) and impressive personalized-marking range unquestionably leading to handwriting-uniqueness judgment. Apparent structural differences fall within graphic-variability. Expert's logical interpretation weighing similarities/differences (not mere listing) revealed structural-similarities from forger-skill successfully imitating morphology while failing imitating ductus scrittorio (slower/controlled signatures). Graphological investigation bases conclusions on dynamic-relationship, hand-movement, speed, fluidity, rhythm (inimitable), not isolated graphic-features. Contemporary-notarial-deed execution-speed differs from will-signatures because different-hand wrote will-signatures. ID: ITI105; Instance_Type: First instance; Legal_Duration: P5Y5M; Law: IT – Civil Code – 602, 606
